transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help with any questions you may have about your cataract surgery recovery. How are you feeling today? Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery that I can help with?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Thanks for reaching out. I'm doing pretty well, but I do have some questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start doing some light gardening, such as brisk walking, gardening, light jogging, and gentle cycling, about 1 week after surgery. However, it's best to avoid strenuous, heavy exercise, lifting heavy objects, pilates or yoga, or swimming for a month. You can also start golf or tennis after 1 week with protective eyewear.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, thank you! My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should continue to use your eye drops as was prescribed. If you're running out, your GP should be able to provide some more. It's safe to use them as directed. Remember to store them as per the instructions on the bottle.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, that's helpful. Another thing I've noticed is that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as it adjusts to the new lenses. If it's mild, just wearing sunglasses when you're outside should help. However, if it's severe or you're experiencing pain, redness, or other concerning symptoms, we may need to assess it further.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, that makes sense. Lastly, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common to have some blurriness, especially in the first week after surgery. But it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the information, Dora. That answers all my questions. I don't have any more for now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It was my pleasure to help. I'm glad I could answer all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery. If you think of anything else, don't hesitate to reach out to your care team for further guidance. Otherwise, I'll just say goodbye for now. .
